sources.title: List of useful console commands - Official TF2 Wiki
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community
Source Dedicated Server - Valve Developer Community (port 27015 carries game traffic and RCON, set with -port)
Source engine banid usage string: banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }
Team Fortress 2 Admin Commands: RCON & SourceMod List

notes: Stock Source-engine admin commands over Valve Source RCON; no plugin required. RCON is not a separate listener - it is TCP on the server's game port (default 27015, set with -port), and it is enabled simply by setting rcon_password in server.cfg, so there is no separate enable setting; the Valve Developer Community's Source Dedicated Server page states that 27015 TCP/UDP carries 'game transmission, pings and RCON'. DURATION IS IN MINUTES, and 0 means permanent: the engine usage string is 'banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }', so {duration} must be rendered as an integer number of minutes. The trailing literal 'kick' is what disconnects an already-connected player - banid on its own only adds the id to the in-memory ban list. BANS ARE NOT PERSISTENT until 'writeid' is run: it flushes the in-memory list to cfg/banned_user.cfg, and that file is only re-applied on boot if server.cfg contains 'exec banned_user.cfg'. The same applies after 'removeid' - run 'writeid' again or the unban is lost at restart. RIFT//CTRL should send writeid as a follow-up to ban and unban; it is not folded into the command strings here because the schema holds one command per field. banned_user.cfg lines look like 'banid 0 STEAM_1:0:38510000' or 'banid 0 [U:1:77020000]', hence the lineIdPattern taking the third whitespace token. PLAYER ID: status prints Steam3 ids, e.g. '#   1039 "BigDickMoe"        [U:1:356612105]     51:17      100    0 active 11.22.33.44:27005', and banid accepts that bracketed form as well as legacy STEAM_0:x:y, so the pattern accepts either. The status userid column is captured as 'userid' - it is the transient per-connection userid (1039 in the sample above), NOT the Steam3 account number (356612105), and it is captured because kickid also accepts a bare userid, which is the safer target for a player whose name contains quotes or spaces. KICKID CAVEAT: kickid is the only command in this file that appears on neither official page - the official TF2 wiki documents only 'kick <name>', and the Valve Developer Community command list carries kick, banid, removeid and say but not kickid. It is attested by RGL ('kickid "[id]"') and by GameServerKings ('kickid <userid> "<reason>"'), and GameServerKings describes it as userid-only; kickid accepting a bracketed Steam3 uniqueid therefore follows the engine's documented 'userid | uniqueid' convention (as seen in the banid usage string) rather than any source that states it outright. If a kick by Steam3 id is ever rejected at runtime, fall back to the captured userid. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: RGL's guide also writes 'ban "[playername]"', which is not a stock Source console command (SourceMod's sm_ban is the likely intent) and was not used here. GameServerKings claims banid takes 'the STEAM_0:1:12345678 form status prints', but status in fact prints the Steam3 bracketed form, so that page is wrong on the detail and the dual-form pattern covers both. A Steam discussion reports 'uniqueid "[U" not found' when a bracketed id was passed through in-game chat rather than the console; sending it over RCON as a single unquoted token avoids that tokenizer split. MOTD: TF2 has no motd console command - the message of the day is the file tf/motd.txt (plus tf/motd_text.txt for the text-only version) and is read at map load, so no motd key is published. 'say' from RCON broadcasts to all players prefixed with 'Console: '.
